extracted.intended_audience: NLP / computational linguistics researchers and practitioners working on Chinese humor generation, recognition, and dataset/model creators
extracted.subtask_description: Developing, evaluating, and releasing a large language model and dataset specialized for Chinese humor tasks (generation, recognition, response selection). Emphasis on dataset compilation, multi-task capability, empirical comparison to popular LLMs, and resource availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task coverage (humor-related tasks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle various Chinese humor-related tasks including Crosstalk Response Selection, Humor Recognition, Joke Generation, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A model should be capable across multiple humor-related task types (response selection, recognition, generation) rather than being specialized to only one. The abstract lists explicit task targets: Crosstalk Response Selection, Humor Recognition, Joke Generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CFunSet dataset comprehensiveness and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a comprehensive Chinese humor-related dataset, the Chinese Fun Set (CFunSet). This dataset aggregates existing Chinese humor datasets and includes over 20,000 jokes collected from Tieba-JokeBar, yielding a corpus of more than 160,000 entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality of dataset is judged by coverage (aggregation of existing datasets), size (20,000+ jokes; total >160,000 entries), and diversity / source documentation (e.g., Tieba-JokeBar). Dataset construction and provenance should be clear and substantial to support multi-task training/evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model performance relative to popular LLMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental results demonstrate that CFunModel outperforms popular large language models in these tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should include empirical comparisons to established LLM baselines on the humor tasks named. Performance improvements (quantitative metrics) over popular models are a central criterion for claiming effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on Chinese-specific humor capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the noted deficiency where most LLMs exhibit poor performance in generating and processing Chinese humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models should be evaluated for language- and culture-specific humor understanding/generation (Chinese). Success criteria include improved handling of cultural/linguistic phenomena particular to Chinese humor, as opposed to generic multilingual capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource availability and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper states 'Our CFunSet is available at [URL] and CFunModel is available at [URL]. A demonstration video of our work is available at [URL].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release of dataset, model checkpoints, and demonstration materials is expected. Reproducibility and public availability of data/model/demos count as quality criteria for research in this area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset aggregation and augmentation practices
rubrics_metrics.description: CFunSet 'aggregates existing Chinese humor datasets' and augments with jokes scraped/collected from online platforms (Tieba-JokeBar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology for aggregating, cleaning, and augmenting datasets (merging sources, deduplication, labeling) is an implicit criterion; thorough documentation of how datasets were combined and curated is required to trust downstream evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration and qualitative validation
rubrics_metrics.description: A demonstration video of the work is provided to illustrate model behavior and capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond quantitative metrics, providing qualitative examples, demos, or videos that showcase generated humor and model responses is considered important for assessing real-world humor quality and user-facing behavior.
